Welcome to the Clinical Trial Application

This application is designed to monitor the preventive efficacy of Pratimarsha Nasya with Anu Taila in adults with Allergic Rhinitis. Below is the complete guide for both Participants (Patients) and Investigators (Doctors).


🟢 PART 1: PARTICIPANT (PATIENT) GUIDE

1. Logging In
Use the unique Patient/Trial ID provided by your investigator to log into the application.

2. Daily Dose Tracking
• Morning Dose: Apply your nasal drops at 8:00 AM. Click the \'Morning Dose\' button to log compliance.
• Evening Dose: Apply your nasal drops at 9:00 PM. Click the \'Evening Dose\' button to log compliance.
Note: Buttons will turn orange if a dose is overdue, and green once successfully logged.

3. Daily Diary
Use the \'Daily Diary\' feature to record any daily notes, mild changes in symptoms, or general wellness tracking for your investigator to review.

4. Reporting a Problem (ADR)
If you experience any Adverse Drug Reactions (e.g., severe burning, headache, nosebleeds), click \'Report a Problem\' immediately. Select the severity and describe the issue. This will instantly alert your investigator.

5. Instructional Video
If you forget how to administer the drops, click \'View Tutorial\' to watch the standardized administration procedure.


🔵 PART 2: INVESTIGATOR (DOCTOR) GUIDE

1. The Monitor Dashboard
The investigator dashboard provides complete oversight of patient adherence, reported problems, and clinical evaluations.

2. Registering a New Patient
Click \'Register New Patient\' to add a participant. Record their demographics, medical history, and trial arm allocation. These details are stored centrally and used to auto-populate clinical forms.

3. Clinical Evaluations & Editing
During Patient Visits (Baseline, Week 1, 2, 4, 8), you are required to submit two forms:
• Nasal Symptom Evaluation: Tracking 5 core symptoms (out of 15) and 3 extended symptoms (out of 24).
• SNOT-22 Health Survey: A comprehensive 22-parameter audit (Total out of 110).

Smart Form Features:
• Auto-Population: Enter the Patient/Trial ID, and the app will automatically load the participant\'s name, age, and gender. These fields are read-only to ensure data consistency.
• Record Editing: Selecting a Visit Interval (e.g., Week 2) will automatically fetch any existing data for that visit. You can modify these records and re-save them as needed.

4. Pulling Patient Records
Enter a Patient/Trial ID and click \'Pull Record\'. The monitor will display:
• Participant Profile: Centralized demographic data.
• Dose Adherence: Calculated percentage and compliance alerts.
• Reported ADRs: Filterable log of safety events.
• Clinical Evaluation History: Itemized scores for Nasal Symptoms and SNOT-22 surveys grouped by visit.

5. Managing Adverse Events (ADRs)
If an ADR is marked as [ACTION REQUIRED], investigate clinically. Once resolved, click \'Mark Pending ADRs as Reviewed\' to clear the queue.

6. Data Auditing & PDF Exports
• Run Audit: Automatically scan for missing timestamps or skipped doses.
• Download PDF: Once a record is pulled, click \'Download PDF\' to generate a formal clinical summary document containing all profile data, adherence logs, and visit scores.


For technical support regarding the application structure or database sync issues, contact the system administrator.
